title: The Silence of the old quarter
premise: Mara Amberdale, a translator who has spent thirty years cataloguing the words their family never spoke, returns to the old quarter when the crumbling house of their childhood is scheduled for auction. Sorting through its rooms, Mara uncovers evidence that a long-ago death in the neighborhood—ruled an accident—was covered up by the very adults who raised them, and that their silence was purchased with the house itself. As demolition looms, Mara must choose between preserving the fragile found family they've built and forcing a reckoning no one wants; in the end, Mara testifies, loses the house but gains the truth, and the found family, tested rather than broken, gathers in the emptied rooms one last time to speak what was never said.
about_author: Theo Okonkwo is the pen name of a former court interpreter who grew up between two languages in a port city's oldest district. Their debut novel draws on years of listening to what witnesses almost said.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In their city apartment, Mara catalogs untranslated words from a dying childhood language, each tied to something unsaid. A letter arrives: the old family house is up for auction in three weeks. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Borrowed Words
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At a translation job, Mara fumbles a phrase only their grandmother used, realizing the language—and the past—is slipping. They decide to visit the house before strangers own it. Emotional beat: grief for what erodes slowly.

chapters.title: The Old Quarter
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara walks streets renamed and repaved, greeted warily by neighbors who remember too much. The house stands boarded, auction notice bright on its door. Emotional beat: the uncanny feeling of being a stranger at home.

chapters.title: Keys That Still Fit
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara breaks in—not quite breaking, since the key still turns—and finds rooms preserved like a held breath. In the kitchen drawer: a ledger in their father's hand, columns of payments. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Weighs
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The ledger records monthly sums marked only 'for the quiet,' beginning the month after a neighbor, Tomas Reyes, died in the yard when Mara was nine. Emotional beat: the floor tilting under everything remembered.

chapters.title: Aunt Vess Knows the Price
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Aunt Vess, keeper of family peace, receives Mara's cautious phone call and lies smoothly, then burns a letter she'd kept forty years. Emotional beat: love weaponized as silence.

chapters.title: The Found Table
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Back home, Mara's chosen family—landlord Dev, exiled poet Sunniva, teenage runaway Kit—notice Mara unraveling over dinner. Kit offers to help 'investigate.' Emotional beat: warmth as anchor against vertigo.

chapters.title: Tomas Reyes Had a Daughter
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara locates Elena Reyes, now a hospice nurse, who agrees to meet but warns: 'My mother stopped speaking that year too.' Emotional beat: two silences recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Elena's Half
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Elena recounts her childhood: her father's death ruled accidental, her mother's sudden muteness, anonymous envelopes that paid their rent until they didn't. Emotional beat: rage arriving decades late.

chapters.title: The Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Kit's POV. Kit, scouting the house, is caught inside by the estate agent, Mr. Calloway, who lets them go with a look that says he knows more than he sells. Emotional beat: fear braided with defiance.

chapters.title: Vess Comes Down From the Hill
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess confronts Mara in person, offering money to drop it—the last payment, she admits, bought the family's silence about what Uncle Bram did. Emotional beat: confession as both wound and gift.

chapters.title: Uncle Bram's Room
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara searches the sealed back room and finds Bram's old tools, bloodstained and buried in lime, wrapped in a shirt Elena would recognize. Emotional beat: physical proof making denial impossible.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Sunniva's POV. Sunniva, once silenced by her own country, argues Mara must speak; Dev argues some truths destroy more than they free. The found family splits. Emotional beat: love strained across an ethical fault line.

chapters.title: The Mother Who Paid
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara visits their mother in care, whose dementia has loosened her tongue: fragments confirm Bram killed Tomas, and the family chose the house over justice. Emotional beat: mourning a parent while indicting them.

chapters.title: Calloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Calloway reveals a developer client will pay well if the sale closes clean, hinting he knows about the ledger and suggesting Mara take the money and forget. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a professional smile.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Kit's POV. Kit photographs the ledger and tools, posts nothing, waits. Someone ransacks Mara's apartment; the ledger copy survives in Kit's backpack. Emotional beat: the cost of knowing becomes physical.

chapters.title: The Reckoning Asked For
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara gathers Vess, Elena, and the dying Bram himself, now frail, and asks the question the whole family arranged itself around: what happened in the yard? Bram neither confirms nor denies—but weeps. Emotional beat: the terrible intimacy of asking.

chapters.title: Fire or Demolition
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The house burns in the night—arson, though no one can prove by whom. Vess suspects her own son; Mara suspects Calloway's developers. Evidence nearly lost. Emotional beat: panic, and strange liberation.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara gives the ledger, the tools, and their testimony to a cold-case detective, knowing Bram may die before trial and the family may never forgive them. Emotional beat: resolve after surrender.

chapters.title: The Verdict of Small Rooms
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Bram confesses on tape before dying; the case closes without spectacle. Vess stops speaking to Mara; Elena begins. Emotional beat: justice arriving quiet, insufficient, real.

chapters.title: Everything Unsaid, Said
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the charred house before clearing, the found family and Elena hold a vigil; each speaks one sentence they'd carried for decades. Mara translates their grandmother's final word aloud at last. Emotional beat: catharsis without absolution.

chapters.title: A New Inventory
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Months later, Mara teaches the dying language to neighborhood children in a rented room above Dev's shop, keeping a new ledger—one that records things said. Emotional beat: survival redefined as speech, not silence.
